title: Unsigned letter to Anne de Montmorency, 1536, BnF fr. 3053 ff. 85-87 with its contemporary decipherment on f. 86 (DECODE R4248; second fr. 3053 cipher)

transcription.notes: 14 Nov 2026: the cipher transcribed sign by sign from the Gallica scans (ark btv1b90601432, views 157-158) into R4248_transcription.txt: 26 lines (12 on f. 85r, 14 on f. 85v), 712 signs measured, 8 marked doubtful; a single AI transcription, not checked by a person, checked by decoding (R4248_decode.md). Sept 2026: about 20 cipher lines (2 on P2, ~11 on P3, ~9 on P5) in a second fr. 3053 cipher, not Mâcon's; then the contemporary clear decipherment on f. 86 (P8-P9) was transcribed (about 85 % of words secure, a few [?]).

system.summary: Substitution on graphic signs with homophones and nulls (30, the triple-barred cross, 22), matching Tomokiyo's second fr. 3053 table (img/francisMacon2.png); not 'Mascon's cipher'.
system.sibling_key: none applied: Tomokiyo's second fr. 3053 table (cryptiana francis.htm) identified as this cipher's; Mascon's cipher tested and gives nonsense.
system.notes: Nulls per Tomokiyo's table: 30, ǂ, 22. Signs seen: ǂ, W, ~, α, ∞, Ɛ, ꝗ, looped ʃ, φ, #, 11, z, k, 30. Not tabulated here: the f. 86 decipherment makes it unnecessary.

prior_solution.where: Contemporary clear decipherment of the passage on f. 86 of the same volume; Tomokiyo notes the f. 85 fragment is 'deciphered on f. 86' (cryptiana francis.htm). No printed plaintext.

conditions.human_role: nothing beyond setting the target; the DECODE session cookie already in the repository served the images

solution.what: Fetched the R4248 page crops (P2-P9) from DECODE with the stored cookie, as part of catalogue item 180 (rome1536).
Applied Mâcon's key (Mascon's cipher, macon_key.md: W = LL, ~ = null, 30 = pape) to f. 85: nonsense.
Matched the glyph set to Tomokiyo's second fr. 3053 table (nulls 30, ǂ, 22; R = W; O = 3; U = α); 'ꭓ m Ɛ 3 30 11 ǂ' after 'et partant' starts JE LE CO[NSEILLOIS] as in the decipherment.
Transcribed the full contemporary clear decipherment on f. 86 (P8-P9), about 85 % of words secure; it agrees with every clear connecting phrase left on f. 85.

Split from rome1536 under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): R4248 is in a second fr. 3053 cipher and was read from its contemporary decipherment, not with Mascon's cipher; its own entry, with R4248.md and Tomokiyo's second table moved here.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): R4248.md (clear-text summary and the transcription of the f. 86 contemporary decipherment); no sign-level transcription of the f. 85 cipher exists in the folder

Looked for a transcription of the f. 85 cipher (audit section I): none in the folder, none on DECODE R4248 (nine images, no text; full-size DECODE images need a login). Fetched BnF fr. 3053 from Gallica through openapi.bnf.fr IIIF (ark btv1b90601432): f. 85r = view 157, f. 85v = view 158, f. 86 = view 159. The server answered HTTP 500 and dropped connections for a while (views above 162 do not exist: the first guess of the view numbers was wrong), then served the views at full size.
Transcribed the cipher sign by sign from the full-size scans with shape labels (R4248_transcription.txt): 26 lines, 712 signs, 8 doubtful. By Claude (session of 14 Nov 2026), not checked by a person.

Checked the transcription by decoding it with one value per label, values from Tomokiyo's second fr. 3053 table where a sign matched it and from the f. 86 decipherment otherwise (R4248_decode.md): all 26 lines come out as French and follow the decipherment. Holes: one word of L16 ('aaiette'), the ringed x where x and 'pape' are expected, two pairs of look-alike signs not told apart (barred oval r/h; reversed c for c and o), a sign with no letter value standing for the cardinal de Lorraine. The decode differs from the September transcription of f. 86 in nine places (e.g. 'dessus vous, qu'est et le scavoir et le pouvoir'; 'par vostre moien reordonner les conditions'; 'toute capitulation de qui ilz vouloient entierement dependre'; 'ung seur fondement'); f. 86 itself was not re-read. No key file written: the values are Tomokiyo's table and the contemporary decipherment, the method stays 'read from existing decipherment'.

outcome.method_basis: The passage was read from the contemporary clear decipherment on f. 86, checked against the clear connecting words on f. 85; the cipher's key was identified (Tomokiyo's second fr. 3053 table) but not applied or tabulated.
outcome.fraction_read_source: The f. 86 decipherment covers the whole cipher passage; R4248.md transcribes it with about 85 % of words secure (a handful marked [?]). No sign-level count.
outcome.notes: Read from the contemporary decipherment on f. 86: the writer, after a day in the country with a cardinal ('Carafe'?), urged that everything, above all the war, pass through Montmorency's hands; the cardinal of Lorraine had conceded too much in his capitulation with the pope. Writer unidentified (no signature on the crops).

texts.label: Unsigned letter to Montmorency, [1536], BnF fr. 3053 ff. 85-87, decipherment on f. 86 (DECODE R4248)
texts.summary: The writer, after a day in the country with 'monsieur le cardinal Carafe(?)', urged him that everything, above all the conduct of the war, should pass through Montmorency's hands and that anything else was 'fumee et vent'; the cardinal seemed persuaded, and said that the cardinal of Lorraine, in his capitulation with the Pope, had conceded things never thought of before, which they meant to undo (so the transcription of f. 86; the decode of the cipher has 'reordonner'). The decryption is the transcription of the contemporary clear decipherment on f. 86 (R4248.md); since 14 Nov 2026 the cipher of f. 85 is transcribed sign by sign and decoded (R4248_decode.md), which differs from that transcription in nine places listed there.
